5... Qf7
{ Back in the game, Black played Qf7, and White is clearly better. This is the first mistake of the game that hands one side a big advantage. }

13. g5 f5 14. h5 Qe8 15. Ne5 b5 16. Na2 Nd5 17. g6 h6 18. Nf7 Qe7 19. Nxh6+
{ White is down material, and has activity for it. } 19... gxh6 20. Bxh6 b4 21.
Bxf8 Qxf8 22. h6 bxa3
{ A serious mistake, and it leaves the opponent winning. Now White is winning. }
23. Qh5 axb2+
{ This is the move that leaves the opponent winning. Now White is winning. }
24. Kb1 Ba6 25. g7 Bxf1 26. gxf8=Q+ Kxf8 27. h7 Bc4 28. h8=Q+ Ke7 29. Q8e8+ Kf6
30. Qhh8+ Kg5 31. Qeh5+ Kf4 32. Rh4#
{ Checkmate. White mates the black king: the attack on the kingside never stopped, and that is what decided the game. }
